name: RIVER THAMES Northfleet
description: Bright light in fairway of Northfleet Hope and Gravesend Reach; red over anchorage in Gravesend Reach and Broadness..

name: Hope Point Fort
description: A single lamp for colliers

name: Mucking Flat
description: On piles; bright East of N.E. by E., red to W.; also red ray toward Blyth buoy to S. ½ E., and red N. of E.S.E. to clear Scars and Chapman Head. Fog Bell

name: Chapman Head
description: On piles. Bright in fairway channel, red over Leigh Middle to N. of S.E. by E. ½ E. A fog-bell

name: Southend Pier-head
description: Red fixed light

name: Sheerness
description: Red gas lt. on N.W. face of fort on Garrison Point. Not vis. S. of N.N.W. bearing

name: Queenborough
description: 1. Two red leading lights on pier 2. A bright lt., vis. through 45°, is shown from beacon on Queenborough Spit, in 6 ft. water, 80 yds. S.W. from Spit buoy

name: Whitstable
description: Bright fixed light on tall chimney

name: NORE LIGHTVESSEL
character: One br. rev. lt. ½ min.
description: In 3½ fathoms at East end of the Nore Sand. Gong; warning gun

name: Girdler Lightvessel
character: One br. rev. lt. ½ min.
description: In 3½ fathoms W. Girdler Sand at W. entrance of Princes Channel. Gong; warning gun

name: Princes Channel Lt.-ves.
description: In 3½ fathoms N. side of channel, between Girdler and Tongue Lightvessels. Gong; warning gun.

name: Tongue Lightvessel
character: Upper br., lower red, fixed lights
description: In 10 fms. at East Tongue Sand; one red ball. Lts. at unequal heights. Gong. Warning-gun. (Run into and sunk in July, 1877. Wreck marked by lt.-ves., 1½ cable N.N.E. from it, and buoy S.S.W. from it. Keep outside buoy and lightvessel)

name: Margate Pier
description: Column at W. end of Pier; also a small green light on Jarvis Jetty

name: Mouse Lightvessel
description: In 4 fathoms, at West end of Sand. Gong; warning gun

name: Maplin Pile Lighthouse
description: Painted red; lt. not vis. over the sand; a br. ray to S. ¾ W. betw. Girdler Lt. & Shivering Sand buoy. Br. lt. shown 13 ft. below main lt. to S.E. by E. ¾ E. over Spit buoy. Fog-bell

name: Swin Middle Lightvessel
description: In 5½ fathoms at West end of Sand. Gong; warning gun

name: Gunfleet Pile Lighthouse
character: One red rev. lt. ½ min.
description: On S.E. side of Sand; keep ½ mile off, and do not pass to North. Fog-bell

name: Sunk Lightvessel
description: In 9½ fathoms; red and bright flash alternately; half ball above ball. Gong; warning gun

name: Kentish Knock Lt.-vessel
description: Has two red balls vertically. In 11 fathoms on E. side of Sand. Fog-horn 5 secs. ev. min.

name: GALLOPER LIGHT-VES.
description: In 20 fathoms on S.W. side of Shoal; lights horizontal. Gong; warning gun

name: NORTH FORELAND
description: White tower 85 ft. high. A strip of red light to E. end of Margate Sand, between N. ¾ E. and N. by W. ½ W.

name: Ramsgate, Tide Lights
character: 1. Red or green light on West pier 2. Green lt. on W. cliff 3. Green lt. on E. cliff 4. Sparkling lt. 10 secs., on East pier
description: 1. Red lt. while more than 10 ft. in entrance, or from 2½h. before, and 3½h. after high water; changed to green lt. when less than 10 ft. 2. Green lt. in one with W. pier lt. leads through Old Cudd Channel 3. Green lt. in one with ditto leads through Ramsgate Channel 4. Visible 5 secs., invisible 5 secs.

name: GOODWIN LT.-VESSEL
description: Off N. end of the Goodwin Sands, in 10 fms. Lt. shows 3 flashes in quick succession, and is obscured for 36 secs. in ev. min. Three masts & balls by day. Gong. Warning-gun

name: EAST GOOWIN LT.-V.
description: About 1½ mile to the eastward of the Goodwin Sands, in 30 fathoms. Half diamond over diamond at mast-head. Gong; warning gun

name: GULL STREAM LT.-VES.
description: On the West side of the Goodwin Sands, in 8 fathoms. Gong; warning gun

name: S. SAND HEAD LT.-VES.
description: Off the South end of the Good[?]in Sands, in 14 fathoms. Fog-trumpet 5 secs. every 2 min.

name: Deal Iron Pier
description: Red light on pier head

name: SOUTH FORELAND
description: In one W. by N., 1,347 ft. apart; in one, clear S. of Goodwin. High lt. cut off on a S.W. by S. bearing. Magneto-electric apparatus

name: DOVER Admiralty Pier
description: Red tower, 30 ft. high, on end of Admiralty Pier. Fog Bell ev. 7½ secs.

name: Dover Harbour
character: One green light Red Tide Lights
description: One red lt. on N. pier while 7 ft.; one red lt. on S. pier while 7 to 10 ft.; two red lts. while above 10 ft. The green lt. at the W. side of entr. to Granville Dock

name: Folkestone Tide Lights
character: 1. Red and bright lts. 2. Green light
description: 1. On S. pier head a red light while 10 ft.; a white light below it when above 16 ft.; when red lt. is blinked occasionally use caution ... 2. On new pier a green light seaward, but white inshore of danger Fog Bell

name: VARNE LIGHTVESSEL
description: In 16 fathoms at West end of the shoal. Gong. Warning-gun

name: DUNGENESS
character: 1. One fixed light 2. One br. flash. lt. ev. 5 secs.
description: 1. Tower with red and white belts, 240 yds. f[?]om extr. of point. Red lt. over W. anchorage northward of W., and red lt. over E. anchorage W. of N.E. by E. ½ E. 2. New tower on extr. of pt. S.S.E. ½ E. 675 ft. from main lt. Fog-horn 5 secs. ev. min.

name: Rye Tide Lights
character: 1. Two bright fixed lts. 2. Two red fixed lights. 3. One green fixed light
description: 1. Camber, on N. side of the entrance while 10 feet; in one N. ½ W. 2. Near old pier head from half flood to half ebb 3. West entrance to harbour half flood to half ebb

name: Hastings
description: On West Hill, in one, N.N.E., 508 ft. apart, to direct the fishermen (Sept. 29 to Mar. 25). A green light on the pier

name: R. SOVEREIGN SHOALS
description: In 12 fms., S. Ely, 2 miles from R. Sovereign buoy. Shows 3 flashes in 23 secs., at intervals of 37 secs. Small ball over usual mast-head ball. Gong. Warning-gun.

name: Eastbourne
description: A green light is shown on the pier, and two red lights on the beach

name: BEACHY HEAD
description: A white lighthouse, 47 ft. high, on summit of Belletout Cliff. From the eastward the lt. will open when bearing N.W. ¾ W., and by keeping it so will lead 1½ mile outside Royal Sovereign Shoals

name: Newhaven
character: One br. fix. lt. and Tide Light Green light on E. pier
description: On West pier-head. Tide lt. below main lt. red betw. 10 and 13 ft., bright betw. 13 and 15 ft., and green above 15 ft.

name: Brighton Chain Pier
description: One green fixed light

name: ,, Pile Pier
description: One red fixed light

name: Shoreham Harbour
character: One bright fixed light, and Tide Light Two green lights
description: Tide lt. on central pier, green while 8 to 11 ft., bright while 11 ft. and over, and red at high water; bears S. by W. ¼ W. from upper lt. Two green lts., one on E., one on W. pier-head. Approaching, keep high br. lt. open E. of W. pier green lt., and when clear of W. pier-head, keep near the pier until high lt. and tide light come in line

name: Worthing Pier
description: Fixed light on the pier

name: Littlehampton
character: Red lt. on E. pier, N. end
description: Also tide lts. on S. end of pier; white 10 feet, green 11 ft., red 12 ft., red & white 13 ft., two white 14 ft., white & green 15 feet, till H.W.

name: OWERS LIGHTVESSEL
description: On the S.E. end of the Owers Shoal, in 19 fms. Flashes twice bright, once red. Fog Trumpet 6 blasts every minute. Warning Gun

name: Nab Lightvessel
description: Near New Grounds; must be passed to eastward. Gong; Warning Gun

name: ST. CATHERINE'S PT.
description: Stone tower, reduced in height in 1875. Lt. vis. between E. ⅞ S. and N.W. ½ W. Fog Trumpet, 2 blasts every 4 minutes

name: Warner Lightvessel
description: In 13 fms., on the eastern part of the shoal. Gong; Warning Gun

name: Ryde Pier
description: A bright fixed light

name: SPITHEAD
description: Green lt. on fort at Brading Haven; red lt. on fort on No Man's Land; white lt. on fort on Horse Sand; red lt. on fort on Spit Sand

name: Stokes Bay Pier
description: Red lights on East and West ends

name: Southsea Castle
description: Shows red in channel between Spit Refuge Buoy and Horse Fort, or to betw. S. by W. and S.W. by S. It is green to West of the Spit Buoy betw. S.W. by S. and W. ½ S.

name: Southsea
description: Two red lights on Clarence Esplanade Pier

name: Portsmouth Dockyard
character: One fixed red or green light
description: On S. end of S. railway jetty. Shows red betw. the eastern side of the harbour and S.E. tangent of Block House fort, and green westward of that line. Harbour railway works will be cleared by keeping in green light

name: Calshot Lightvessel
description: Off Calshot Castle, in 3½ fathoms. Gong; Warning-gun

name: Netley Pier
description: One fixed green light to be shown

name: Southampton
character: 1. Two fixed red lts. 2. Two fix. green lts. 3. One fixed red lt. 4. Two fix. bright lts.
description: 1. On either side of entrance to Docks. In one N.N.E. ¾ E. lead up River Itchen in 15 ft. 2. On Extension Quay, N.W. side of R. Itchen 3. From Harpy lt.-ves., at entr. of Riv. Itchen 4. From iron posts on Royal Pier, 15 yards apart. In one lead up channel

name: Yarmouth
description: Green outer lt. near castle wall; inner br. lt. In one S.S.W. lead into the harb. Temporary lt. on end of wooden pier constructing

name: Needles Outer Rock
character: One fixed bright, or red light
description: Shows red to S. from S.E. ½ S. to W.; then bright over entrance of Needles Channel to W.N.W.; thence red up the ch[?]nnel to N.E. by E., and then bright to N.E. by E. ½ E., to clear Warden Ledge. A bell in fogs

name: Hurst Beach
character: Two bright fixed lights (Low lt. in New Fort)
description: In one N.E. by E. ½ E., 670 feet apart. Another light in the lighthouse shows only up the Solent

name: Poole
description: In one, N. ½ W., 786 feet apart on North side of entrance; also four lights inside

name: Weymouth
description: Two red lts. near beach, E. of railway station Two green lights on North pier

name: PORTLAND
character: High lt., br. and fixed Low lt., br. and fixed
description: White towers, 50 & 85 ft. high, 1,509 ft. apart, near the Bill. In one, N.W. by N., lead betw. Race and Shambles. Low lt. only shown between N.W. by N. ¾ N. and E.S.E.

name: Portland Breakwater
description: Shown from centre of fort at end of Breakwater. Lt. obscured by peninsula between S.S.W. & W. by S. ½ S., & betw. W. by S. ½ S. & W.N.W. lt. is obscured to an observer 15 feet above the sea when within 2 miles of Chesil Bank. Fog Bell

name: Shambles Shoal Lt.-Ves.
description: On E. end of shoal, in 15 fms. Fog Horn, 1 blast every 2 min. Warning Gun

name: Lyme Regis
description: In one, N.W. ½ N., 825 ft. apart. A bright leading light in centre of channel, N. ¼ W.

name: Teignmouth
description: One on a limestone tower on S.W. end of Denn; the other on a house

name: Brixham
description: Red lt. at end of breakwater. Green lt. at end of W. pier. Entering by night, keep N. of Shoalstone Point to open red lt. on inner pier, which leads clear of breakwater

name: Torquay
character: One red, one br. fix. lt.
description: Bright light on inner pier, showing red to westward; red light on outer pier

name: Dartmouth
character: 1. One fixed bright red or green light 2. One bright fix. lt. 3. One small bright, red, or green light
description: 1. On Kingswear or N. side; br. lt. towards fairway, between S. ¾ E. and S. by E. ½ E.; thence red lt. to the land, and green lt. to S.W., between S. ½ W. and the land, or over Checkstone, Pin Rock, &c. 2. S. ¾ E. 110 ft. from former; in one leads up fairway 3. Near Coast-guard Station; br. in fairway, red over shoals on N. side of harbour. and green lt. over shoal of One Gun Point to S.

name: START POINT
character: One brilliant revol. lt., visible every minute
description: A white tower, 92 ft. high. A fix. lt. at 181 ft. is also vis. from tower over Skerries Rocks betw. N.E. ¾ E. and E. ½ N. Fog Horn, 1 blast every 3 minutes

name: Plymouth Breakwater
character: One bright or red light Lower bright light
description: On W. end; red to seaward, but br. E. of N.E. ½ E. from it. A lower br. lt. is seen when the channel is open. A bell during fogs ...

name: Plymouth Harbour
description: On W. Barbican pier-head is shown a br. lt., a red lt. on Millbay pier-head, & also one at Mt. Wise landing. Fog-bell, 8 strokes a min.

name: EDDYSTONE
description: An admirable stone tower, with red and white bands, 89 ft. above foundation on the rock, which covers 14 ft. at high water. Fog-bell, 5 strokes once in every ½ minute

name: Falmouth
character: One rev. lt. 20 secs. Lower fixed light One green fixed light
description: On St. Anthony Pt. The lower lt. to S.S.W. over Manacles Rocks, between S.S.W. ½ W. and S. by W. ¼ W. Fog-bell struck 4 times in every alternate ½ minute. On Prince of Wales breakwater

name: LIZARD
description: Two white towers, each 61 ft. high, W. by N. & E. by S., 223 ft. apart, on the Lizard Cliff. In one lead clear of the Manacles. A signal and telegraph station on Beast Point, about ¾ of a mile to E. Fog-trumpet, 1 blast every 5 minutes

name: WOLF ROCK
description: A noble granite tower. Flashes red and white alternately. Fog Bell, 3 strokes ev. ¼ min.

name: Penzance Tide Light
character: A fixed red or br. light, while 15 ft. inside; green while less
description: On the S. pier-head. Shows red to E. by S. ¾ S. to S. by W. ¼ W. The remainder a bright light. By day, a ball while 15 feet

name: LONGSHIPS
description: New tower, 1873. White lt. seaward, from N.N.E. ½ E., or ½ mile W. of Brisons Rocks, to S. by E., or ¾ mile W. of Runnelstone; red in-shore of these bearings. Fog-bell 2 strokes ev. ½ minute

name: SEVEN STONES LT.-VES.
description: On E. side of rocks, in 40 fms.; two red balls; Warning-gun; powerful Fog-horn ev. 10 secs. or Gong. To be altered in summer of 1879 to rev. lt., showing 3 flashes once in ev. min.

name: SCILLY
character: One bright revol. light every minute
description: A white tower, 74 feet high, on the summit of St. Agnes' Island; obscured by islands from N. by E. to East

name: BISHOP ROCK
description: On the S.W. rock. A noble stone tower, 147 feet high. Invisible to eastward between N.E. by E. and E. by S. ½ S. Bell ev. 10 secs.

name: St. Ives Tide Light
description: On the pier head. Lighted from Sept. 1 to April 30. Also a red light on end of outer wooden pier

name: Hayle Tide Lights
character: 1. Two fixed bright lts. 2. One fixed red light
description: 1. On W. side of entr.; in one S.S.W. ½ W., 297 ft. apart, while 12 ft. water 2. On jetty of Lelant Quays

name: GODREVY
character: One br. flash. lt., 10 secs. Lower red light
description: On the island. A bell in fogs. Lower red lt. to N.W. over the Stones Rocks, between N.W. and N. by W.

name: Padstow
description: A red or green light on quay head

name: TREVOSE HEAD
description: The lower light is 50 feet to seaward of the upper

name: HARTLAND POINT
description: New tower, showing at intervals of 30 secs. two bright and one red flash. Fog-Horn 5 secs. in every 2 min.

name: LUNDY ISLAND
character: Upper lt., rev. ev. 2 m. Lower fixed light
description: In one tower, 96 ft. high. Low light visible to W. between N.N.W. and W.S.W. Rocket every 10 min. in fogs

name: Bideford
description: On Braunton Sands, North side of entrance. In one, S.E. ¼ S., lead over bar; from half flood to half ebb

name: BULL POINT
description: Lt.-ho. to be completed during the summer of 1879, and will show triple flash. lt. ev. ½ min. A lower red fix. lt. will be shown over Morte Stone. Fog-trumpet, to give 3 blasts once every 2 minutes

name: Ilfracombe
description: One red light on Lantern Hill

name: Watchet Breakwater
description: Tide light fixed, 8 ft. flood to 10 ft. ebb

name: Burnham, or Bridgewater
character: Up. lt. intermit. 4 min. Lower light fixed
description: In one, E. by S. ½ S., 1,500 ft. apart. Low lt. bright, visible westward from W. by N. to N.W. by W. ¾ W.; a red lt. from low tower shows over the bar from W. by N. to W. ½ N.; and a red lt. up the river from S. by W. to S. by W. ½ W.

name: Cleveden
description: Red light on pier-head

name: Portishead
description: Bright light on pier

name: Breaksea Lightvessel
character: One br. rev. lt. 15 secs. One red fixed light
description: In 8 fms. 2 miles W. by N. ½ N. from One-fathom Bank buoy; one ball; red lt. shown from after part. Gong; signal gun.

name: Avon
description: White tower, 65 ft., on the E. side of channel. a red sector to N.W., and a green ray from W. to W. by S. at turn of channel

name: English & Welsh Grounds Lightvessel
description: On S. side of Bristol Channel, in 14 fathoms; a red ball, gong, gun, &c.

name: New Passage
description: Lights on pier and Charstone Rock for railway steamers

name: FLATHOLM
description: On South point. Light is red from S. ¼ E. to N. by W. ½ W.

name: Briton Ferry
description: North side of dock entrance; red light when passage is clear; green light when not open

name: Usk, Newport
description: West side. Light bright in channel, red over Welsh Grounds and Welsh Hook; bright North to land; bright up river

name: Cardiff
description: About 23 yards apart. One on pier-head

name: NASH POINT
character: Two bright fixed lights One red light
description: White towers 1,000 ft. apart, S.E. by E. ½ E., and N.W. by W. ½ W. Red light from high lighthouse from N.W. by W. ½ W. to N.W. ½ W.

name: Porthcawl
character: One br., two red tide lts.
description: On ends of breakwater

name: Swansea Harbour
character: 1. One red fixed tide lt. 2. One fixed bright lt. 3. Two green or red lts. 4. Two green or red lts.
description: 1. White tower on W. pier-head; shown while 8 ft. water. Fog-bell; black ball by day ... 2. Additional bright lt. shown 430 yds. from extreme of W. pier, visible only to eastward 3. At South dock, vertically 4. At North dock, horizontally, red when closed, green when open

name: Scarweather Sand Lt.-V.
description: Off W. end of Sand, in 14 fms. A half globe above usual globe. Fog-trumpet, 2 blasts once in every 2 minutes. Signal Gun

name: Mumbles
description: A white tower. 56 ft. high, adjoining the fort

name: Helwick Lightvessel
description: In 16½ fathoms, off W. end of Sand. Fog-horn 5 secs. ev. 2 min. Warning-gun

name: Llanelly
description: One on Whiteford Point (on piles) from ½ flood to ½ ebb; from ½ flood to ¾ ebb on S. end of breakwater

name: Burry Port
description: Near head of W. pier while 10 feet water

name: Saundersfoot, South Pier
description: One red light or yellow ball while 8 feet

name: Tenby Pier Head
description: One red tide light for steamers, &c.

name: CALDY ISLAND
character: One br. or red fixed lt.
description: The lt. is bright seaward, but is red toward Old Castle Head, from N. 70° W. to N. 56° W., and is red over Woolhouse Shoal from N. 55° E. to N. 15° E.

name: ST. ANN'S POINT
description: White towers, 75 and 42 ft., 610 ft. apart, on W. side. In one N. by W. ½ W., lead in clear of Crow and Toes Rocks. A red ray from high lighthouse shows over Chapel and Harbour Rocks to between S.E. ½ S. and E. ½ S. Fog Horn, 1 blast every 3 minutes

name: Great Castle Head
description: In one, N.E. by E. ¾ E., lead in mid-channel

name: Pembroke Dockyard
description: Two red lts. in one lead up. High lt. shown betw. W. by N. ¾ N. & N.W. ¼ N. Low lt. betw. W. by N. ½ N. & N.N.E. A green sector betw. N. ¼ W. and N. by W. ¼ W. is shown over Carr Spit

name: Neyland Pier
description: Bright light near end of landing pier; red lt. occasionally on railway pier

name: SMALLS
description: Granite tower, 141 ft., red & white bands. Lt. bright seaward, from E. ½ S. to S.E. ½ E. The lt. is red over Hats and Barrels Rocks. Bell sounded, and rockets to explode sent up ev. half hour in fogs.

name: SOUTH BISHOP ROCK
description: A white tower, 36 feet high. A Gong in fogs. Fog-trumpet proposed

name: New Quay
description: On pier-head. To southward of E. ½ S. the light is red

name: CARDIGAN BAY LT.-V.
description: In 35 fathoms, at 20 miles northward from Port Cardigan Gong

name: Aberystwith
character: One fixed light Two bright fixed lights
description: Harbour entrance, lt. red to S. and W., bright to N.W. and N.E. Two lts. in a field, over inner end of harbour, while sufficient water

name: St. Tudwall Roads
character: 1. One br. and red lt. 2. One lower red lt.
description: 1. Vis. 8 secs., obscured 2 secs. White to westward betw. N. by E. and S. by W. Red from S. by W. to S.E. White from S.E. to N.E. by E. ½ E., and thence red to N. by E. Obscured by East Island, betw. N.E. ½ E. and E. by N. ½ N. 2. A ray with an arc of 15° is shown over Carreg-y-trai, from E. by S. to E. ½ N., from window 16 ft. below main light

name: BARDSEY ISLAND
description: A square white tower, 99 ft. high. Fog Horn, 1 blast every 5 minutes

name: Llanddwyn Point
description: A red light all night

name: Caernarvon
description: One bright light on pier-head

name: CAERNARVON BAY LT.-VESSEL
description: In 30 fathoms, at 12½ miles S.S.W. ¾ W. of South Stack light-ho. Flashes bright, bright and red. A small ball over large one. Fog Horn, 1 blast every 2 minutes

name: SOUTH STACK ROCK
description: White tower, 84 ft. During fogs, a smaller br. revol. lt., at 40 ft., is shown at 30 yds. N. of lt.-ho. A Fog-bell once ev. 15 secs.; also Gun (experimental, with holophone mouthpiece) fired ev. 10 min. from North Stack

name: Holyhead
character: 1. One red flash. lt. 7½ s. 2. One bright fixed lt. 3. One small red light 4. Red and green lights
description: 1. Lighthouse on new breakwater. Fog Bell 3 times every 15 secs. Fog Horns for mail packets at 11 a.m. and 11.30 p.m. 2. On end of wooden jetty; old harbour Bell. 3. On old tower, to N.E., shown from N.E. to N.N.E. ½ E. to clear Platters. Fog Bell 4. Red lt. on starboard; green lt. on port side of inner harbour

name: SKERRIES
character: One bright fixed light Lower red light
description: Upper lt. not visible over East Platters Rock, from S.S.E. to S.E. ½ S. Red lt. over Ethel and Coal Rocks, from E. ½ S. to E. by N. ½ N. Fog Horn, 1 blast every 3 minutes

name: Amlwch Port
description: On North pier; shown only when the harbour is practicable

name: LYNUS or ELIAN POINT
description: A white building, 36 ft. high. Light visible 8 secs.; eclipsed 2 secs. Masked to mark Middle Mouse and Dulas Rocks

name: Beaumaris
description: Bright light on pier

name: Menai, Trwyn-Du Point
description: Circular building, 96 ft. Large Fog Bell thrice every 15 secs.

name: GREAT ORMES HEAD
description: Light bright from N.W. by W. ¾ W. to E., red from E. to E. ¾ S.

name: Llandudno
description: Green light on pier-head. Lower red lt. when it is dangerous to come alongside

name: Rhyl
description: Bright light on pier-head

name: AIR POINT
character: One br. or red fixed lt.
description: On old lighthouse, with red and white bands. It is red only within Hoyle Sand, from N.W. to E. by S. ¼ S.; fog-bell

name: N.W. LIGHTSHIP
character: One br. rev. lt. ½ min.
description: In 13 fathoms N.W. ¼ W. 8½ miles from Horse Channel Fairway Buoy; a blue lt. every 2 hours; a black ball. In fogs, a bell

name: BAR LIGHTVESSEL
description: North 9½ miles from Upper Hoylakelt.-ho., & N.W. by W. ¼ W. 8¾ miles from Crosby lt.-ho. Fog-horn 3 times a minute or Bell

name: Hoylake
description: White towers, 55 and 31 ft. In one, S.W. ¾ S., 1,200 ft. apart, near the church

name: Leasowe
description: On the shore, between the Mersey and Dee

name: BIDSTON
description: A stone tower, 68 ft. high, on the hill; masked to N. by E. ½ E.

name: ROCK
character: One rev. br. lt. ½ min.
description: A white tower, 94 ft. high. Also a fixed lt., while 11 ft. down Rock Channel; and another up the Mersey, from same tower. Fog-bell

name: North Docks Wall
description: Bright betw. S. by W. & N. by W. ¾ W., red over Formby Bank E. of N. by W. ¾ W. In line with Rock lt., bearing E. ¼ S., indicates turning point betw. Horse & Rock Channels

name: Birkenhead New Pier
description: One bright fixed light

name: Formby Lightvessel
description: At the elbow of Crosby and Queen's Channels, in 50 ft. Hull black. Fog-bell

name: Crosby Lightvessel
description: In 48 ft., off the N.E. elbow of the Burbo Bank; a red ball. Fog-horn 3 times a min., or Bell

name: Crosby Lighthouse
description: Square tower, 74 ft., near the point

name: Ribble River
character: One intermittent light One bright Tide Light
description: S.E. of Stanner Point; visible 3½ min.; dark ½ min. Tide lt. on new pier, from 2h. before to 1½h. after high water

name: Lytham Harbour
description: One fixed light, while the approach is practicable

name: Blackpool Pier
description: Green light seaward; bright to land

name: Fleetwood
description: North and South, 850 ft. apart; shown while 9 ft. Fog Bell, 3 strokes every minute

name: Wyre River
description: Pile lt.-ho. on N.E. end of North Wharf bank. Fog Bell

name: Lune River
description: On Cockerham Point and Plover Scar Rock, while 8 ft. water

name: Clark Wharf Spit Lt.-Ves.

description: S.W. headland of Cantyre

description: A fixed white light on pier-head

description: Lt.-ho. on S.W. end of Holy Id., E. side of S. entr. to harbour. Vis. seaward from S.E. ½ E. to S.W. by S., and in harbour. Fullerton Rock W. ¾ S. 530 yards from lighthouse

description: In 18 fathoms, 3½ miles S.E. by E. from N. end of bank; has 3 masts, lights, and globes, on main and fore. Gong. (To be altered in spring of 1879 to revol. lt., showing 2 flashes once in every minute.

description: On pier-head. Red to seaward, from S.S.E. to N.E.; br. lt. obscured betw. S. ½ E. & shore

description: One fixed bright light
